Make it rain. Make Snow. Make Earth Habitable. 

Rainmaker builds and deploys audacious technologies that work with nature to create an abundant, habitable planet. We are building an integrated system to make more freshwater available to farms, ecosystems, and communities.

Our ambition is bold, but we pursue it with humility. We take on difficult problems in the real world with technical rigor, grit, integrity, and an openness to learning and course-correcting. We are hiring individuals with evidence of exceptional ability. If you want to build systems that endure, restore, and deliver the future we were promised, we want to hear from you.

 The vehicle software team builds the software that operates Rainmaker’s cloud-seeding vehicles, connecting flight control, onboard computing, sensors, payloads, and ground operations. We work closely with electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, and flight operations teams to turn new hardware into reliable systems that can be built, deployed, and operated at scale. Our goal is to make every vehicle a dependable tool for delivering more freshwater where it is needed.

About the Role 

 - You will own embedded firmware across Rainmaker’s vehicle and its integration with our onboard and ground control software systems. Your scope includes flight-controller firmware, power distribution, sensor and payload controllers, and the interfaces connecting those systems to onboard Linux software. You will take work from architecture and board bring-up through testing, manufacturing, deployment, and support in the field. We’re looking for a high-agency engineer who identifies what needs to happen, turns incomplete requirements into a clear plan, and follows through until the hardware works reliably in real operating conditions. This is a hands-on technical ownership role with the autonomy to shape the firmware architecture and the responsibility to deliver it.

What You'll Do

 - 

 - Own the architecture, implementation, and maintenance of all embedded firmware across the vehicle, including flight-controller firmware, power distribution, sensors, and seeding payloads.

 - Set firmware priorities, identify reliability risks and technical gaps, and drive projects from an ambiguous problem to a validated release.

 - Bring up new boards with electrical engineers: read schematics, validate interfaces, write drivers, and debug failures at the boundary between hardware and software.

 - Develop dependable device communication and command handling over CAN, UART, SPI, and I2C, with clear contracts for telemetry, timing, and fault behavior.

 - Integrate firmware with our vehicle software so commands, device state, and telemetry behave consistently from the microcontroller to the operator.

 - Design and validate safe startup states, watchdogs, interlocks, and recovery behavior for resets, communication loss, sensor faults, and interrupted updates.

 - Own firmware builds, versioning, flashing, over-the-air updates, and recovery workflows so deployed vehicles run known, traceable software.

 - Build automated tests, simulation, and hardware-in-the-loop coverage that catch regressions and exercise failure modes before releases reach the fleet.

 - Partner with manufacturing and flight operations to make provisioning, calibration, diagnostics, and servicing repeatable and practical.

 - Investigate bench and field failures using logs, telemetry, and lab instruments; resolve root causes and turn what you learn into better software and tests.

What We're Looking For

 - 

 - 3+ years of hands-on experience developing embedded software or firmware for microcontroller-based systems, including board bring-up, hardware integration, and deployment into production or field use.

 - Demonstrated ownership of an embedded subsystem from design through release and ongoing support, including making technical decisions independently, validating behavior on hardware, and resolving failures in real operating conditions.

 - Strong systems programming skills in Rust and/or C/C++, with the ability and willingness to work across both Rust and C/C++ codebases.

 - Practical experience with peripheral drivers and communication buses such as CAN, UART, SPI, and I2C.

 - Comfort reading schematics and using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and hardware debuggers to isolate problems across electrical and software boundaries.

 - The ability to reason about system failures and implement robust state machines, fault detection, safe outputs, and recovery paths.

 - Experience building maintainable firmware with version control, reproducible builds, automated testing, and disciplined release practices.

 - Evidence of high agency: you surface problems without waiting to be assigned, make sound decisions with incomplete information, ask for help when it matters, and close the loop on results.

 - Clear communication and the ability to work closely with hardware engineers and operators, explain tradeoffs, and document decisions so others can build and service what you ship.

What Will Set You Apart

 - 

 - Experience with drones, robotics, aerospace, or other systems where software controls physical equipment in demanding conditions.

 - Familiarity with PX4, MAVLink, flight-controller development, or flight-critical software.

What Success Looks Like In the First 90 Days

 - You have mapped the vehicle’s firmware, hardware interfaces, build and update paths, and most consequential reliability risks, and the team has a clear plan for what to address first. You can independently build, flash, instrument, and debug the key embedded systems and trace their behavior through our vehicle software. You have delivered a meaningful firmware improvement through bench and integration testing into an operational release, working with flight operations to verify its behavior in the field. You have improved at least one recurring source of friction in testing, provisioning, updates, or diagnostics, and established a practical ownership and release cadence for the firmware stack.

Supporting the Rainmakers behind the mission

Making earth more habitable is ambitious work and we want the people doing it to feel supported:

 - A stake in what we build: Meaningful stock options and the opportunity to help shape Rainmaker as an early member of the team. 

 - Support for your health: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and your family. 

 - An investment in your future: A 401(k) with employer matching to help you build long-term savings. 

 - Time to recharge: Unlimited PTO for rest, exploration, and the people and pursuits that matter to you plus a generous paid holiday schedule. 

 - Time for a growing family: Paid parental leave for both parents to welcome a child and spend time together. 

 - Lunch together: Daily lunch provided at our El Segundo headquarters, giving Rainmakers a chance to share a meal and connect with teammates. 

 - Help making the move: Relocation assistance for eligible roles to support your transition to Rainmaker.

At Thesis, we believe everyone should have the opportunity to meet their potential. We build nootropic supplements and customer experiences that help people find the right support for their goals.
Across Thesis and Stasis, we're also changing how our company works. Our teams use AI to develop creative, research customers, build digital experiences, analyze performance, and reduce repetitive operational work. We're looking for an engineer who can turn those experiments into reliable systems that people use every day.
About the Role
We're looking for an AI Engineer to build the agents, integrations, and internal tools that help a small team accomplish more. You'll work with Data, Engineering, Growth, Creative, and Operations to find valuable problems, prototype solutions, and own them through deployment, adoption, and ongoing improvement.
This is a hands-on software engineering role focused on applied AI. You'll build with existing models, connect them to our tools and knowledge, and make their outputs useful and trustworthy. You should be as comfortable debugging an API integration as designing an agent workflow, and care about whether your work saves time, improves decisions, or helps the business grow.
We already have AI-assisted workflows and a shared Claude skill and knowledge system. You'll build on that foundation, making successful workflows easier to reuse and bringing production engineering to the parts that need it. You won't be starting from a blank page, and you won't be limited to maintaining what's already there.
How You'll Make an Impact
Build agents that do useful work
Design and ship agents that retrieve information, use tools, and complete multi-step tasks across our business systems.
Connect workflows across tools such as Slack, Google Workspace, Asana, Shopify, and Klaviyo through APIs, webhooks, and MCP integrations.
Make long-running workflows dependable with persistent state, retries, duplicate prevention, clear approvals, and recoverable failures.
Accelerate creative and growth workflows
Partner with Creative and Growth to improve the path from customer research and performance insights to briefs, scripts, creative variants, and testable landing pages.
Build workflows that combine brand knowledge, approved product claims, asset libraries, and creative performance data while keeping human review where it matters.
Help teams learn from prior experiments so each new brief or test benefits from what we've already discovered.
Make company knowledge and data more useful
Extend our shared skills, knowledge base, retrieval, and context-management systems so AI tools can find and use the right source material.
Partner with our data team to connect AI workflows to governed analytics in Metabase and Hex, backed by Snowflake, rather than inventing competing definitions of business metrics.
Use SQL and data validation to investigate issues, verify outputs, and make analytical workflows easier for non-technical teammates to use.
Turn prototypes into reliable products
Build evaluations using real business tasks. Test accuracy, task completion, tool behavior, failure recovery, latency, and cost before scaling a workflow.
Add monitoring, useful logs, version control, automated tests, and clear documentation. Own failures after launch and fix their causes.
Protect customer and company data, separate brand and account contexts, and preserve human approval for consequential actions.
Choose the simplest approach that works, including ordinary code or deterministic automation when an LLM adds no value.
Help the company use AI well
Work directly with teammates to understand their workflows, ship usable interfaces, and help them adopt what you build.
Create reusable skills and integrations rather than isolated prompts that only their author can operate.
Evaluate new models and tools through practical experiments, then explain what is worth adopting and why.
Measure outcomes such as time saved, adoption, output quality, and faster experiment cycles, not just the number of automations shipped.
We're Excited About Your
Experience shipping software that real users depend on, with ownership beyond the initial prototype.
Hands-on LLM application development using Anthropic, OpenAI, or comparable APIs, including structured outputs, tool calling, retrieval, and multi-step workflows.
Strong Python or TypeScript skills, sound software design, and comfort working with APIs, authentication, databases, and asynchronous jobs.
Practical understanding of RAG, context management, and MCP. You can explain the tradeoffs and show when a simpler approach is better.
Ability to build evaluations, diagnose unreliable behavior, and improve an AI system using evidence rather than prompt tweaking alone.
Working SQL proficiency and experience validating data against established reporting or warehouse models.
Product judgment and clear communication. You can turn an ambiguous request into a focused solution, explain technical tradeoffs, and work effectively with non-technical partners.
Curiosity, initiative, and follow-through. You experiment independently, learn quickly, and take responsibility for whether your work is useful.
Experience with Claude Code, Codex, shared agent skills, or agent orchestration platforms such as OpenClaw is a plus. So is experience with ecommerce, consumer subscriptions, creative production, multimodal generation, or analytics tools such as PostHog and Metabase. We don't expect you to have used every tool in our stack.
How You'll Work
You'll work on problems with visible business impact, from reducing manual reporting to making creative production and customer research more effective. You'll partner closely with the people doing the work, test with real inputs, and keep improving the system after it ships.
We value people who can move quickly without confusing a convincing demo with a dependable product. Bring strong engineering fundamentals, good judgment about where AI helps, and a willingness to get into the details.
In Your Application
Tell us about an AI system you built that people actually use. What problem did it solve, what did you personally build, how did you evaluate it, and what failed along the way? Share a demo, repository, or architecture walkthrough where possible. Please don't include confidential information from another employer.

Competitive compensation and equity.
Health, dental, and vision plans.
HSA, FSA, and pre-tax commuter benefits.
401k to help you plan for the future.
Flexible PTO.
Unlimited Thesis nootropics.
A strong emphasis on personal development and promoting from within.
A dog-friendly office in Flatiron, near Union Square and Madison Square Park.
Our Values
Meet Your Potential: Keep learning, seek honest feedback, and help others grow.
Own Outcomes: Take responsibility for results, act with urgency, and follow through.
Lead with Science and Data: Seek the truth through evidence and use it to make better decisions.
Create Exceptional Experiences: Show up for teammates and customers with care, high standards, and a sense of belonging.
Pay Transparency
Our salary ranges reflect competitive compensation for our size and industry and are one part of a total rewards package that includes benefits and equity. **Thumbtack helps millions of people confidently care for their homes.**
Thumbtack is the one app you need to take care of and improve your home — from personalized guidance to AI tools and a best-in-class hiring experience. Every day in every county of the U.S., people turn to Thumbtack to complete urgent repairs, seasonal maintenance and bigger improvements. We help homeowners know which projects to do, when to do them and who to hire from our growing community of 300,000 local service businesses. If making an impact inspires you, join us. Imagine what we’ll build together.
  
  
**About The Business Applications Team**
The Business Applications org builds and operates the internal systems that keep Thumbtack running at scale: Salesforce-centered workflows, admin tooling, and the integrations that connect teams across the company. We're now expanding that foundation into a broader internal platform for AI-enabled work — shared APIs, reusable integration patterns, and safe, auditable capabilities for business-critical actions. We work directly with the business teams who depend on these systems, turning complex operational needs into software that's easier to run, extend, and automate responsibly.
  
  
**The challenge**
Agents can already take action inside Thumbtack's internal systems. The harder problem is making that trustworthy: giving business teams a way to configure what agents are allowed to do, review and correct their work, and see clearly what happened and why. Without that, automation stays stuck in pilots. This engineer owns the product surface that turns agent capability into something teams will actually rely on for business-critical work — and the services behind it.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Design and build the interfaces business teams use to configure agents, review their work, approve or correct actions, and understand what happened and why.
* Build observability and evaluation tooling that makes agent behavior legible — where it succeeded, where it failed, and whether a change made things better.
* Work across the stack, from React and TypeScript through service code and data models, owning features end to end through build, test, launch, and iteration.
* Partner directly with the business teams who use what you build; translate ambiguous operational problems into working software.
* Own the full lifecycle of your work, including monitoring and post-launch improvement.

**In order to be successful, you must bring**

* 3+ years of professional software engineering experience.
* Strong frontend skills with React and TypeScript, including complex application state and data-dense interfaces.
* Solid backend engineering ability. We use Go, PHP, and Python, and we expect strong engineers to pick up a new language.
* Working knowledge of relational and non-relational data stores (Postgres, DynamoDB, or similar).
* Real product judgment: you can look at a workflow, decide what to build, and say what to cut.
* Interest in the problems that come with non-deterministic systems — uncertainty, partial failure, and designing for human correction rather than assuming a correct answer every time.
* Proven ability to navigate ambiguity, close your own knowledge gaps, and deliver in an evolving environment.
